diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, for any $i$ and using the same formula as above, by choosing a test function $\phi$ which is equal to one on $\bm{x}_i$ and 0 on all the other $\bm{x}_j$, it is easily checked that $|T^{-1}(\{\bm{x}_i\})|=v_i$.

issues.failure_explanation: The identity $T\#\mathrm{Leb}=\hat{\mu}$ only implies that $T^{-1}(B)$ is Lebesgue-null for every Borel set $B$ disjoint from $\{\bm{x}_i\}$; it does not prevent $T$ from mapping a null set to points outside $\{\bm{x}_i\}$. Counterexample: for $N=1$, $v_1=1$, $\bm{x}_1=0$, the map $T(x)=0$ for $x\neq 1/2$ and $T(1/2)=7$ satisfies $T\#\mathrm{Leb}=\delta_0=\hat{\mu}$ but its image $\{0,7\}$ is not contained in $\{0\}$. The correct statement is containment up to a Lebesgue-null set. The lemma's conclusion $|T^{-1}(\{\bm{x}_i\})|=v_i$ is unaffected, since it follows directly from $T\#\mathrm{Leb}(\{\bm{x}_i\})=\mathrm{Leb}(T^{-1}(\{\bm{x}_i\}))$.

failure_location.quote: Reciprocally, if $T\#\mathrm{Leb} = \hat{\mu}$ then by choosing a test function whose support does not contain any $\bm{x}_i$, one can see that the image set of $T$ is contained in $\{\bm{x}_i\}_i$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claim by: the image of $T$ is contained in $\{\bm{x}_i\}_i$ up to a Lebesgue-null set (equivalently, work with maps defined only up to equality almost everywhere); the rest of the proof is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Only the justification inside the proof is affected; the lemma's equivalence (partition map iff pushforward with masses $v_i$) remains valid up to null sets, and every downstream use (the semi-discrete formulation and the Laguerre cells) is unchanged.
issues.title: Lemma lem:added-1: the claim that the image of T is contained in {x_i} is false for general measurable maps
issues.why_classification: The false intermediate claim admits a one-line measure-theoretic correction ('up to a null set'); the lemma's conclusion and all of its uses remain valid, so no substantive claim or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The intersection of two Laguerre cells has zero Lebesgue measure and the weights $w_i\in \mathbb{R}$, called Kantorovich potentials, are uniquely defined such that for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\},
In particular, although the result is valid for very general cost functions, most applications consider the $L^2$ cost function

issues.failure_explanation: The stated hypotheses allow degenerate costs: $c\equiv 1$ is $C^{1,1}$ and takes values in $[0,+\infty)$. For such a cost every partition map attains the same minimal value, so the Monge problem has infinitely many solutions; moreover the Laguerre cells $\mathscr{L}_i=\{x: w_i\ge w_j\ \forall j\}$ satisfy $|\mathscr{L}_i|\in\{0,1\}$, so no weights realize $|\mathscr{L}_i|=v_i\in(0,1)$ when $N\ge 2$. Hence both the asserted uniqueness of $T$ and the existence of the volume-constrained weights fail. The cited results (bourne_semi-discrete_2018, kitagawa_convergence_2019) assume a non-degeneracy condition, e.g. that the sublevel sets $\{c(\cdot,\bm{x}_i)\le t\}$ have Lebesgue measure tending to $0$ as $t$ decreases to $\inf c(\cdot,\bm{x}_i)$; this hypothesis was omitted. Every cost actually used in the paper (power, $L^2$, cost-shape) satisfies it.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a standard non-degeneracy hypothesis to Theorem thm:semidiscrete, e.g. for each $i$ the sublevel sets $\{c(\cdot,\bm{x}_i)\le t\}$ have Lebesgue measure tending to $0$ as $t\downarrow\inf c(\cdot,\bm{x}_i)$; this is satisfied by every cost used in the article and requires no other change.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem as stated is false for degenerate costs. Because all experiments use strictly radially increasing costs, the model, the discrete solver, and all numerical results remain valid once a standard non-degeneracy hypothesis is added; lemma:prefferedshape (self-contained proof) and lemma:celldoublet (quadratic cost only) are not invalidated.
issues.title: Theorem thm:semidiscrete: uniqueness of the Monge solution and existence of the Kantorovich weights fail for degenerate (e.g. constant) costs
issues.why_classification: The counterexample is a degenerate case excluded by a standard one-line hypothesis already present in the cited literature; the conclusion, method, and advertised scope for all costs actually used are preserved, so the repair is local and lossless.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \begin{equation}\label{eq:perturblong}f(\delta) = -\delta_+,\end{equation} which corresponds to lowering the potential and thus allowing deformations in the directions of large nonnegative gradients.
This corresponds to a larger cost in the direction of larger gradient but even larger for negative gradient.

issues.failure_explanation: The cell shape is the sublevel set of the cost $c$ (Lemma lemma:prefferedshape), equivalently a superlevel set of $\varphi=-\log c$. With $f(\delta)=-\delta_+$, the potential is lowered where the chemoattractant gradient is positive, which raises the cost $c=c_0 e^{-\beta f}=c_0 e^{\beta\delta_+}$ in that half-space and therefore shrinks the cell there; the cell extends opposite to the gradient. The same holds for $f=\delta_-^2+\delta_+$, which lowers the cost on both sides, more strongly opposite to the gradient. Since $\dot{\bm{x}}_i=-\tau\nabla_{\bm{x}_i}\mathcal{T}_{c_0}(\hat{\mu})$ moves each centroid toward the barycenter of its own cell, the written perturbations drive the particles away from the attractant -- the opposite of the claimed chemotactic migration. The fan description is also inverted: for $f=\delta_-^2+\delta_+$ the cost is smaller, not larger, in the direction of larger gradient, and even smaller for negative gradient. The root is a sign confusion between $c$ and $\varphi=-\log c$: the shape is a superlevel set of $\varphi$, whereas the classical level-set analogy invoked in the text (and the sentence 'lowering the potential ... allowing deformations') corresponds to sublevel sets.

failure_location.quote: Since the morphological changes are biased in the direction of increasing gradient, this choice induces chemotactic migration.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the sign convention between the potential and the cost -- change $\varphi=-\log c$ to $\varphi=+\log c$ (equivalently, flip the signs of both perturbation functions) -- and re-derive the described deformation types, re-checking Fig. fig:chemotaxis and the two chemotaxis videos; the framework itself needs no modification.
issues.overall_effect: The subsection's central advertised phenomenon -- chemotactic migration induced by gradient-biased shape deformations -- is not delivered by the written construction; the deformation descriptions ('elongated'/'fan-like', 'in the direction of increasing chemo-attractant gradient'), Fig. fig:chemotaxis, and SM Videos video:chemo_long and video:chemo_fan are unreliable as written and must be re-verified against a corrected sign convention. The rest of the paper is unaffected.
issues.title: Chemotaxis subsection: the perturbation signs produce deformations biased away from the chemoattractant, so the claimed chemotactic migration fails as written
issues.why_classification: As written, the model produces the opposite of the advertised phenomenon, and the source does not reveal whether the text or the implementation carries the wrong sign, so the figure and videos require re-verification; the fix is contained (a sign convention plus re-derivation of the deformation taxonomy) but is more than a routine one-line correction because two non-equivalent repairs exist and the 'fan-like shapes orthogonal to the gradient' description survives neither.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: that is, protrusions are created randomly and naturally retract.

issues.failure_explanation: An unreflected Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process $d\xi_k=-\xi_k\,dt+dB^k_t$ is a Gaussian process that takes negative values with positive probability at all positive times, whatever its initial condition, so it cannot satisfy the stated constraint $\xi_k\ge 0$. The model as written is therefore ill-posed: either the constraint is violated by the dynamics, or the SDE must be understood as a reflected (Skorokhod) OU process, which the source does not state.

failure_location.quote: We assume that the elongation range (amplitude) of the protrusion $\xi_k$ is constrained by $\xi_k\geq0$ and follows the stochastic differential equation

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the amplitude equation as a reflected Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process on $[0,\infty)$ (Skorokhod reflection at $0$); this standard one-line modification enforces $\xi_k\ge0$ and preserves the intended creation-retraction behavior.
issues.overall_effect: The protrusion model's amplitude dynamics are not well defined as stated; the qualitative description (random creation and retraction of protrusions) and the resulting motion are unaffected once reflection at zero is imposed.
issues.title: Random protrusions: the nonnegativity constraint on the OU amplitudes is incompatible with the stated SDE
issues.why_classification: A standard local repair (reflection at zero) makes the dynamics compatible with the stated constraint and preserves every qualitative claim; no result or guarantee is lost.
